What We Do

Full-Service Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Revenue Cycle Management

OMS billing requires simultaneous management of dental procedure codes (D-codes) and medical CPT codes, precise dental-medical crossover routing, and prior authorization for orthognathic surgery that spans dental and medical benefits. PMEX manages both claim streams inside your existing OMS practice workflow.

Dental-Medical Crossover Routing

Procedures with medical indication routed to medical insurance alongside dental claims.

Orthognathic Surgery Billing

Jaw surgery CPT codes (21141 to 21196) billed with medical necessity and orthodontic documentation.

Facial Trauma Coding

Facial fracture repair, soft tissue laceration, and reconstruction codes billed from the operative report.

Dental Implant Billing

Surgical implant placement codes billed to medical insurance when tooth loss has a medical etiology.

TMJ Surgery Billing

TMJ arthroscopy and open joint surgery coded to medical insurance with correct diagnosis codes.

Anesthesia Coordination

Anesthesia billing coordinated with surgical claims for in-office general anesthesia cases.

Common OMS Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Orthognathic surgery denied because orthodontic treatment documentation was not included in the auth.

PMEX compiles orthodontic and surgical documentation before submitting every jaw surgery prior authorization.

Medical insurance never billed for procedures with a documented medical indication.

PMEX identifies every OMS procedure with a medical etiology and submits coordinated dental and medical claims.

Facial trauma claim denied because injury documentation does not establish the traumatic cause.

PMEX confirms trauma documentation including date of injury, mechanism, and clinical findings before billing.

PMEX codes in-office OMS anesthesia from the anesthesia record using correct time unit calculation.

Implant surgical claim not submitted to medical insurance when cancer or trauma was the cause of tooth loss.

PMEX reviews implant cases for medical etiology and submits to medical insurance when the indication supports coverage.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in OMS Billing

OMS practices lose 18 to 32 percent of revenue to crossover routing errors, orthognathic authorization failures, and anesthesia coding mistakes.

PATTERN 01

Orthognathic Surgery Denied, Orthodontic Records Missing

Jaw surgery prior authorization submitted. Medical payer denies: orthodontic treatment records demonstrating that surgery is required for functional correction were not included. Surgery delayed. $8,000 to $20,000 surgical fee at risk.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX compiles the complete orthognathic surgery authorization package: cephalometric analysis, orthodontic treatment records, surgical treatment plan, and documented functional impairment before submitting the authorization.

PATTERN 02

Medical Insurance Not Billed for Medically Indicated Extraction

Tooth extraction performed on a patient with documented cardiac valve disease requiring pre-surgical dental clearance. Only dental insurance billed. Medical insurance, which covers medically necessary dental extractions in this context, not billed. $180 to $420 per extraction in medical revenue not pursued.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX identifies dental extractions with documented medical indications and submits coordinated dental and medical claims with the correct CPT code and medical necessity diagnosis on the medical claim.

PATTERN 03

TMJ Surgery Billed to Dental, Denied as Excluded

TMJ arthroscopy billed to dental insurance as a dental procedure. Dental plan excludes TMJ treatment. Medical insurance, which covers TMJ arthroscopy as a musculoskeletal procedure (CPT 29804), was never billed. Revenue lost.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX routes TMJ arthroscopy and open joint procedures to medical insurance using the correct orthopedic CPT codes and musculoskeletal diagnosis codes, not to dental insurance where TMJ is typically excluded.
